source: Alfei, Miller, Ryan, Urcelay (2025) Rethinking Memory Impairments: Retrieval Failure
finding: Most amnesic-manipulation deficits can be reversed by the right retrieval cues. Amnesic treatments create new learning that interferes with the original memory, so recall depends heavily on cues.
numbers: Psychological Review, DOI 10.1037/rev0000538. Scopus citations listed: 6. Abstract page only.
limits: Only the abstract page was read. The machine mapping below is ours.
agent_relevance: Treat a missing answer as a possible cue failure, not lost knowledge. Try a different cue before concluding the agent does not know.

source: Zheng et al. (2025, ICLR) Spurious Forgetting in Continual Learning of Language Models
finding: LLM performance on old tasks collapses after new training but the knowledge is still there. The loss is in task alignment, not knowledge. Closest LLM twin of amnesia as retrieval failure.
numbers: Task 0 accuracy falls from near 100% to about 10% within 150 steps of Task 1. Recovery probe (fine-tune on half of Task 0, test the other half) stays near 100%, 96% at end of Task 1.
quote: performance on older tasks could be restored by training on merely ten safety instances or irrelevant tasks
limits: Synthetic biography data plus some real continual-learning sets. The recovery probe uses half of old-task data, so it is a cue of a sort.
agent_relevance: Dropped skills may be cue loss. A small re-alignment prompt or few examples could restore them.

source: Zheng et al. (2025) Spurious Forgetting: safety alignment case
finding: LLaMA-2-7B-Chat safety fell to 0% after fine-tuning and returned with ten harmful-refusal examples. Irrelevant data restored old behaviour.
numbers: AdvBench safety: 100% to 0%, then about 99% after ten epochs on ten safety instances.
limits: One model, one benchmark, ten examples.
agent_relevance: A few cue examples can restore a whole behaviour. Test cue-restoration before rewriting a scaffold.

source: Zheng et al. (2025) Freeze strategy
finding: Freezing bottom layers protects task alignment. Replay of 20% old data did not undo the misalignment well.
numbers: SEQ accuracy 11% to 44% on Biography with Freeze; other methods peaked at 22%.
limits: Weight-level fix, not usable by a prompt-only agent.
agent_relevance: Interference acts at the input side of the network, like a cue-mapping fault.

source: Lucki et al. (2025, TMLR) An Adversarial Perspective on Machine Unlearning for AI Safety
finding: Supposedly unlearned hazardous knowledge in Zephyr-7B returns with unrelated fine-tuning, direction ablation or adversarial prefixes. Unlearning hides access; it does not erase.
numbers: WMDP-Bio base 64.4%. Unlearned RMU 29.9%, NPO 29.5%, DPO 27.9%. Finetune on 10 unrelated retain samples: NPO 52.7%, DPO 57.0%, RMU 61.6%, MMLU loss under 2 points. 1000 samples fully recovers.
limits: Single 7B model. Logit-lens could not decode RMU answers, so RMU does remove some residual-stream information.
agent_relevance: Direct machine analogue of amnesic treatment plus a recovery cue. Suppression is not deletion.

source: Lucki et al. (2025) orthogonalization and prefixes
finding: Removing an unlearning direction or adding a universal prefix restores answers.
numbers: RMU orthogonalization 64.7% vs 64.4% baseline. Universal prefixes lifted RMU 29.9% to 53.9%, NPO 29.5% to 46.0%, DPO 27.9% to 49.0%.
limits: White-box methods. Prefix optimised on 6 questions.
agent_relevance: A short cue prefix can reopen access. Cue search is a cheap probe.

source: Lucki et al. (2025) dose-response of cue size
finding: More unrelated cue examples give more recovery. Five forget-set samples nearly restore RMU.
numbers: 10 retain samples partial recovery; 1000 retain samples full recovery; 5 forget-set samples near original for RMU.
limits: Weight finetuning, not prompting.
agent_relevance: Recovery grows with cue amount. Start small and scale.

source: Hu et al. (2025, ICLR) Unlearning or Obfuscating? Benign Relearning
finding: Small, loosely related benign text makes unlearned LLMs output the unlearned content again. Fits the view that the trace stays and only the route is cut.
numbers: Relearning on public medical or wiki-style text restores WMDP hazard answers and verbatim Harry Potter text. Keyword search attack passes 70% success. Relearn set built for 15 WMDP questions without direct answers.
limits: Gradient-based unlearning methods only (GA, GD, KL, NPO, SCRUB). Per-method numbers not recorded here.
agent_relevance: Related, non-identical context is enough as a cue. Priming context can matter more than the exact fact.

source: Gekhman et al. (2025, COLM) Inside-Out: Hidden Factual Knowledge in LLMs
finding: Models hold more answer knowledge inside than they say. An internal scorer ranks correct answers above wrong ones more often than output probability does.
numbers: Average relative gap 40% across three LLMs. In 56% of questions, 1000 sampled answers were all wrong. In 9% of questions the internal scorer still ranked the true answer first though the model never generated it in 1000 tries.
quote: fail to generate it even once, despite large-scale repeated sampling of 1,000 answers
limits: Closed-book QA, three models, authors' own knowledge definition.
agent_relevance: Storage is not the bottleneck. Retrieval or generation is. Repeated sampling cannot fix some cue failures. A different cue or an internal scorer might.

source: Orgad et al. (2025, ICLR) LLMs Know More Than They Show
finding: Models can encode the correct answer in hidden states and still output a wrong one. Truthfulness signals sit in specific tokens and do not transfer across datasets.
numbers: Error taxonomy covers 96% of TriviaQA errors for Mistral-7b-instruct. Error detector fails to generalise across datasets.
limits: Probing needs white-box access.
agent_relevance: Wrong answers do not prove missing knowledge. Resample and re-cue before accepting.

source: Berglund et al. (2023) The Reversal Curse
finding: Models trained on 'A is B' fail on 'B is A'. Retrieval depends on the direction of the cue, as encoding specificity predicts. Facts are stored but reachable from one side only.
numbers: Fine-tune: 96.7% on description-to-name, 50.0% name-to-description, about 0% on reversed. Llama-1 above 80% QuestionToAnswer, below 7% AnswerToQuestion.
limits: Fails in parametric memory only. Works when the fact is in context.
agent_relevance: Put the cue in the same form as the encoding. Offer both directions in memory notes.

source: Berglund et al. (2023) Reversal Curse: GPT-4 celebrity test
finding: Real-world check of the reversal curse in a deployed model.
numbers: GPT-4 names the parent 79% of the time, the child 33%. Ten tries per question, success if correct at least once. A second set gave 28% on Child.
limits: Authors note prompt sensitivity.
agent_relevance: Retry with reworded cues. Success rises with variety.

source: Berglund et al. (2023) Reversal Curse: in-context fix
finding: The curse does not apply when the fact sits in the prompt. Putting the fact in context removes the retrieval gap.
numbers: Appendix B.6: models deduce the reverse relation in context.
limits: Not tested in agent memory stores.
agent_relevance: A scratchpad that restates facts in both directions works as a cue.

source: Allen-Zhu & Li (2023) Physics of Language Models 3.1: Knowledge Storage and Extraction
finding: Perfect memorisation of biographies does not mean the facts can be extracted by questions. Extraction needs varied expressions (paraphrase, shuffle, translation) in pretraining. This is encoding variability.
numbers: Without augmentation, QA accuracy on held-out people is near 0% regardless of instruction fine-tuning. Mixed training gives 86.6% OOD on bioS single, 77.7% on bioR single. Linear probes find the attribute on the name token only with augmentation.
limits: Synthetic biographies, small models trained from scratch.
agent_relevance: Write memory entries in many forms and with many cue handles so later queries can reach them.

source: Allen-Zhu & Li (2023) extraction failure and scale
finding: Failure holds even when the model is 7000x larger than N = 100k people.
numbers: Result 2: perfect token memorisation plus perfect QA for half the people gives no correct QA for the other half.
limits: Synthetic setup.
agent_relevance: Scale alone does not give access. Cue format does.

source: Liu et al. (2024, TACL) Lost in the Middle
finding: Models use facts at the start and end of context but miss the middle. Position acts as a retrieval cue. Same information, different access.
numbers: Multi-document QA U-shaped curve. GPT-3.5-Turbo can drop over 20 points. At 20 and 30 documents it falls below the 56.1% closed-book score. Claude-1.3 closed-book 48.3%.
limits: 2023 models. Later long-context models reduced but did not remove this.
agent_relevance: Place key facts at context edges. Do not stuff context with unranked memory.

source: Liu et al. (2024) longer context does not help
finding: Extended-context versions did not fix the middle problem.
numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) 56.0% closed-book vs 56.1% base. Retrieval and reordering gave only small gains (about 1-1.5 points reported for some settings).
limits: Older models.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on window size to solve access.

source: Wang & Sun (2025) Unable to Forget: Proactive Interference in LLMs
finding: Retrieval of the latest value falls log-linearly as earlier updates to the same key pile up. Errors are old, overwritten values. Humans show the same proactive interference.
numbers: Accuracy falls toward 0 as updates per key go from 3 to 400, with 46 keys. Telling the model to forget or ignore old content gave only marginal gains. A task-goal meta-prompt did not remove the trend.
quote: Attempts to mitigate interference via prompt engineering yield limited success
limits: Synthetic key-value stream. Slope differs by model size.
agent_relevance: Interference, not storage, limits memory. Prune or overwrite stale entries rather than asking the model to ignore them.

source: Wang & Sun (2025) input-length control
finding: Interference load, not prompt length, drives the decline. Holding length constant still shows the drop.
numbers: A control with fixed input length keeps the effect.
limits: Exact control numbers not copied.
agent_relevance: Count competing similar entries per cue, not just tokens.

source: Park et al. (2023, UIST) Generative Agents
finding: Agent memory stream retrieves by recency, relevance (embedding cosine) and importance. Retrieval scoring is the cue design. Removing memory, planning and reflection hurts believability.
numbers: TrueSkill: no reflection or planning mu=25.64; crowdworker 22.95; no memory, planning or reflection 21.21. Full architecture vs prior work d=8.16. Kruskal-Wallis chi2(4)=150.29, p<0.001. 100 raters.
limits: Rated believability in a simulation, not accuracy. Memory embellishments occur.
agent_relevance: Weight cues by relevance plus recency plus importance. Reflections add higher-level cue handles.

source: Park et al. (2023) memory retrieval function
finding: Final score is a weighted sum of min-max normalised recency (exponential decay), importance (LLM rated 1-10) and relevance (embedding cosine). All weights set to 1.
numbers: Importance example: mundane event 1, asking crush on a date 8. Top memories that fit the window are used.
limits: Weights not tuned.
agent_relevance: Direct template for cue scoring in our agent.

source: Packer et al. (2023) MemGPT
finding: Paging memory in and out of context with search functions lets the LLM re-cue its own archive. Multi-step search is the retrieval-cue loop.
numbers: Deep memory retrieval accuracy: GPT-3.5 Turbo 38.7% to 66.9% with MemGPT; GPT-4 32.1% to 92.5%; GPT-4 Turbo 35.3% to 93.4%.
limits: Task built by the authors from Multi-Session Chat. Fixed-context baselines.
agent_relevance: Letting the agent issue its own cue queries to memory is a large win.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion
finding: Verbal self-reflection stored as episodic text is retrieved next trial and changes behaviour. A written lesson is a cue for later retrieval.
numbers: ALFWorld: ReAct+Reflexion completes 130 of 134 tasks. HumanEval pass@1 91% vs GPT-4 80%. ReAct-only gains halt between trials 6 and 7.
limits: Depends on the reflection being right.
agent_relevance: Store and re-read short lessons.

source: Xu et al. (2025) A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
finding: Linked notes with keywords, tags and context descriptions are rewritten as new memories arrive. More cue handles per memory. Tested on LoCoMo.
numbers: LoCoMo has 7,512 QA pairs, 9K-token dialogues. Compared with LoCoMo, ReadAgent, MemoryBank, MemGPT by F1 and BLEU-1. Margins not extracted (table garbled).
limits: Margins not recorded.
agent_relevance: Several cue attributes per memory; evolve links.

source: Zheng et al. (2025) recovery probe design
finding: Their test: fine-tune on half the old-task data, test the other half. Lost knowledge gives near 0 recovery; kept knowledge gives near 100.
numbers: Recovered Task 0 ACC uses exact match. Plain Task 0 ACC uses first-token accuracy.
limits: Needs training access.
agent_relevance: Prompt-only version: give few-shot cues from the same task and measure.

source: Synthesis across LLM lines
finding: Five LLM lines (spurious forgetting, unlearning recovery, hidden knowledge, reversal curse, extraction needing augmentation) all show lost access is not lost storage. No cited work links to the amnesia literature; the link is ours.
numbers: 96% recovery (spurious forgetting); 52.7-61.6% from 10 samples (unlearning); 9% of questions with true answer ranked first yet never sampled in 1000 tries.
limits: Different tasks and models. Mapping is interpretive.
agent_relevance: Design rule: on failure, change the cue first, then add content.

source: Gap: no direct LLM test of the Alfei et al. 2025 claim found
finding: Search budget ran out and arXiv, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar APIs returned HTTP 429, so a direct test was not found. Absence is not proof.
numbers: 0 successful WebSearch calls.
limits: Coverage of 2025-2026 may be incomplete.
agent_relevance: Re-run later with cue-dependent plus agent memory queries.
